sources.title: Disruptor: High performance alternative to bounded queues for exchanging data between concurrent threads

credibility_signals.evidence: Discloses design, benchmark topologies, JVM, operating systems, processors, message counts, and measurement choices
credibility_signals.review_status: Industry technical paper; not peer reviewed

freshness_signals.assessment: Old benchmark environment; single-writer, preallocation, sequence, and cache-contention mechanics remain relevant

sources.selection_rationale: Directly informs bounded rings, stable single-writer ownership, cache-aware state, sequencing, dependency graphs, and explicit latency benchmarking.
sources.notes: Authors: Martin Thompson, Dave Farley, Michael Barker, Patricia Gee, Andrew Stewart. Problem: contention and latency in asynchronous pipelines. Method/result: preallocated bounded ring and sequence barriers; authors report higher throughput/lower latency than Java queues. Caveats: vendor-authored, Java-specific, 2011 hardware, best-of-three metrics are not portable Market Squawk evidence. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events

credibility_signals.method: Empirical NYSE TAQ study of 50 randomly selected S&P 500 stocks
credibility_signals.open_version: Full paper and journal metadata on arXiv

freshness_signals.assessment: Foundational online-feature evidence; venue and asset calibration must be refreshed

sources.selection_rationale: Provides a simple incremental order-flow-imbalance feature, empirical depth-conditioned impact result, and explicit limitations useful for online features and slippage controls.
sources.notes: Authors: Rama Cont, Arseniy Kukanov, Sasha Stoikov. Method: regress short-interval price changes on top-of-book OFI. Result: linear OFI-price relation with impact inversely related to depth. Caveats: one month, 50 U.S. stocks, Level I data, potential explanatory-variable tautology, deeper-book effects omitted. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: ABIDES: Towards High-Fidelity Multi-Agent Market Simulation

credibility_signals.authors_institutions: Georgia Tech, University of Georgia, and J.P. Morgan AI Research

freshness_signals.assessment: Mature discrete-event architecture; empirical market fidelity remains illustrative

sources.selection_rationale: Supports deterministic discrete-event order, protocol-shaped messages, configurable network latency, interacting agents, and counterfactual response beyond static replay.
sources.notes: Authors: David Byrd, Maria Hybinette, Tucker Hybinette Balch. Method: message-driven multi-agent discrete-event simulator modeled on ITCH/OUCH. Result: demonstrates tens of thousands of agents and example market-impact experiments. Caveats: preliminary/illustrative validation, simplified background agents, examples trade one symbol on one exchange. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Bridging the Reality Gap in Limit Order Book Simulation

credibility_signals.author_signal: Includes recognized market-microstructure researcher Mathieu Rosenbaum
credibility_signals.evidence: Method and multiple stock/strategy case studies exposed

freshness_signals.assessment: Very current, not peer reviewed at cutoff

sources.selection_rationale: Current practical recipe for calibrated event timing, imbalance state, impact decay, strategy-sensitive execution cost, and P&L simulation.
sources.notes: Authors: Patrick Noble, Mathieu Rosenbaum, Saad Souilmi. Method: projected spread/volume-imbalance state, calibrated timing, signed-flow power-law feedback. Result: reports realistic concave impact, reversion, and execution-parameter sensitivity. Caveats: v1 preprint, large-tick assets/several stocks, projected state omits full-book detail, cross-asset replication open. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Look-Ahead-Freedom as Temporal Non-Interference: A Verifiable Correctness Property for Backtesting and Agentic Trading Pipelines

credibility_signals.method: Formal calculus, soundness argument, explicit decidability boundary, and artifact claim
credibility_signals.review_status: Listed as submitted to ACM TOSEM; not peer reviewed at cutoff

sources.selection_rationale: Directly formalizes reference-time versus availability-time semantics for windows, resampling, joins, point-in-time reads, and vintage reads.
sources.notes: Author: Xavier Fonseca. Result claimed: sound linear-time check over a value-independent fragment; full data-dependent availability case is undecidable. Caveats: single-author nine-day-old v1, no peer review, artifact not independently reproduced, decidable fragment excludes data-dependent availability. Use as provisional test/property inspiration. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Survivorship Bias in Performance Studies

freshness_signals.assessment: Old empirical context; survivor-selection mechanism remains durable

sources.selection_rationale: Supports historical constituents, delisted instruments, membership-as-of data, and explicit universe selection instead of present-day survivor sets.
sources.notes: Authors: Stephen J. Brown, William Goetzmann, Roger G. Ibbotson, Stephen A. Ross. Method: analytical/numerical study of samples truncated by survival. Result: truncation can create apparent predictability. Caveat: mutual-fund setting and older period; does not prescribe instrument/corporate-action schemas. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: The probability of backtest overfitting

credibility_signals.provenance: Official publisher page with method and result summary

sources.selection_rationale: Adds strategy/model-selection risk controls that point-in-time data, chronological splits, and realistic execution do not solve alone.
sources.notes: Authors: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Qiji Jim Zhu. Method: combinatorially symmetric cross-validation to estimate probability of backtest overfitting. Result: reasonable PBO estimates in examples. Caveats: does not fix leakage, survivors, fill realism, fees, or regime mismatch; trial set must be preserved. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: On the coherence of Expected Shortfall

credibility_signals.provenance: Full arXiv manuscript with journal reference
credibility_signals.method: Formal comparison of risk-measure definitions and coherence

freshness_signals.assessment: Foundational mathematical result; implementation edge cases remain current

sources.selection_rationale: Defines coherent ES under discontinuous/discrete loss distributions and exposes ambiguity in naive tail-mean implementations.
sources.notes: Authors: Carlo Acerbi, Dirk Tasche. Result: identifies an ES definition coherent for general distributions and estimable where usual VaR estimators can fail. Caveat: theory does not choose horizon, scenarios, dependence, confidence level, or finite-sample method. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Optimal execution of portfolio transactions

freshness_signals.assessment: Foundational baseline with simplified price/impact dynamics

sources.selection_rationale: Makes volatility risk, temporary/permanent impact, schedule, implementation cost, and liquidation tradeoffs explicit for a testable paper-execution baseline.
sources.notes: Authors: Robert Almgren, Neil Chriss. Method/result: mean-variance execution framework and explicit efficient frontier under linear impact. Caveats: no queue priority, venue fragmentation, partial fills, rejects, cancels, fees, latency, or state-dependent liquidity. Baseline only, not a realistic paper broker. Accessed 2026-07-15.

sources.title: Convergence in Motion: A Review of Fair Value Levels' Relevance

credibility_signals.disclosure: IASB-linked funding/research context and limitations disclosed

freshness_signals.assessment: Post-IFRS 13 synthesis; not itself a current standards text

sources.selection_rationale: Direct evidence for treating hierarchy level, input observability, model risk, measurement-process complexity, value relevance, and data quality as distinct explained dimensions.
sources.notes: Authors: Andrei Filip, Ahmad Hammami, Zhongwei Huang, Anne Jeny, Michel Magnan, Rucsandra Moldovan. Result: Level 3 is less value relevant overall than Levels 1/2, with change over time; model/process complexity may contribute. Caveats: value relevance is not classification correctness; small Canadian interview component; IASB funding disclosed; not a rules engine. Accessed 2026-07-15.
